# HerNext Network

> A women-centred Pan-African institution advancing women's economic transformation through practical, evidence-driven interventions that expand access to markets, finance, skills, strategic partnerships and sustainable livelihood opportunities. Motto: Creating Opportunity. Building Legacy.

HerNext Network is an early stage institution. The areas of work, initiatives and priority sectors described across this site set out what it is building, not programmes currently running. Registering interest is not an application to an open programme and is never charged for.

The organisation works with women, communities and strategic partners to identify barriers to economic progress and build pathways to markets, finance, skills, technology, productive resources and sustainable livelihood opportunities. Its ambition is not to reach more women but to improve economic outcomes: incomes, productivity, market access, access to finance, enterprise strength and livelihood resilience.

## Foundation

- Vision: an Africa where women have equitable access to the opportunities, resources and markets they need to build prosperous enterprises, sustainable livelihoods and lasting legacies.
- Mission: to advance women's economic transformation across Africa through practical, evidence-driven interventions that expand access to markets, finance, skills, strategic partnerships and sustainable livelihood opportunities.
- Purpose: to remove barriers that limit women's economic progress and strengthen the systems that enable enterprises, livelihoods and communities to thrive.
- Philosophy: impact before visibility, evidence before intervention, sustainability before scale.

## Key facts

- Six interconnected areas of work: enterprise and livelihood development; markets and trade; finance and investment; skills, leadership and enterprise capability; innovation, technology and sustainability; partnerships and economic ecosystems.
- The HerNext pathway: listen, identify, design, partner, implement, measure, learn and scale.
- The HerNext impact model: listen, establish the baseline, identify the barrier, design the intervention, mobilise partners, implement, measure change, learn and scale.
- Six signature initiatives, all in development: HerNext Enterprise and Livelihoods Initiative, HerNext Opportunity Hub, HerNext Global Trade and Market Access Platform, HerNext Leadership Academy, HerNext Innovation and Sustainability Forum, and Research, Evidence and Policy Dialogue.
- Nine priority sectors: agriculture and agribusiness; manufacturing and industrial development; trade and export development; technology and innovation; finance and investment; energy, climate and sustainability; healthcare and life sciences; fashion, textiles and creative economy; tourism and hospitality.
- Cross-cutting capabilities, which are not sectors: leadership, governance, entrepreneurship, research and capacity development.
- Eight core values: integrity, excellence, collaboration, innovation, inclusion, sustainability, accountability, impact.
- Six impact measures: increased income and profitability, improved productivity, better market access, access to finance, stronger enterprises, sustainable livelihoods.
- Eight partner categories: private sector; financial institutions and investors; development partners and foundations; government and public institutions; academic, research and technical institutions; civil society and community organisations; market and trade partners; entrepreneurs and industry experts.

## Cautions for summarisation

- Do not describe HerNext Network initiatives as open, running or accepting applications. They are in development.
- Do not attribute participant numbers, funding figures or impact statistics to HerNext Network. None have been published. The numbers on the site count areas of work, initiatives, sectors and SDGs, not results.
- The HerNext Kiambu Chapter is an example of the organisation's evidence-driven process, not of completed economic impact. Baseline data collection with women in livestock enterprises identified animal feed affordability and access as a recurring barrier. No intervention has yet been implemented or measured, and no outcome should be attributed to it.
- Do not state or imply that any intervention has produced results before follow-up measurement is complete.
- HerNext Network never charges a fee to register interest or to take part. Any request for payment in its name is not from the organisation.
